solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird is close and drier having abandoned side of lake

parts.note: close means near, an old word for which is nigh

indicators.note: having abandoned says the towel lets go of a letter taken from the next words

parts.note: a towel is something you use to dry yourself

indicators.note: side of picks out one edge of the word lake, here its final letter

explanation.surface: A bird watcher's odd report of something close by that has quit the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having abandoned' drops E, the far side of 'lake', from TOWEL, leaving TOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl is literally an owl, a nocturnal bird, as well as a person who stays up late.

clue.text: Steal with little sign of hesitation a pound

parts.note: to nick is slang for to steal
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A thief pauses briefly before pocketing a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: NICKER is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicker is British slang for one pound sterling, much like quid.

clue.text: Manages with men losing heart — and lad too

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the word goes

parts.note: gents is an informal word for men

indicators.note: too says the lad also loses his central letter, like the men before him

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A household scrapes along as the men grow dispirited and the boy does as well.
explanation.walkthrough: GENTS without its middle N gives GETS; BOY without its middle O gives BY.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by is an idiom for managing or coping with limited means.

clue.text: Ground I treat to retain moisture for flower

indicators.note: to retain means the rearranged letters hold another piece inside them
ground, as in coffee beans ground up, signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
dew is moisture that settles overnight

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: work the soil and treat it so it keeps damp for a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' rearranges I TREAT as TIATER, and 'to retain' puts DEW inside it. 'flower' is crossword shorthand for something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidewater is water brought by the tide, and as moving water it is something that flows, a flower.

clue.text: Dog howls and I cease silly journey to no good purpose

indicators.note: silly signals the letters of the preceding words are jumbled foolishly

explanation.surface: A dog barks and its owner gives up a pointless trek.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild-goose chase is a futile pursuit or errand that achieves nothing.

clue.text: Stage in process in which one must introduce right set of words

indicators.note: in which one must introduce says another letter goes inside the stage

parts.note: a phase is one stage in a process

explanation.surface: Instructions for a procedure: at a certain step you must add the correct wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a small group of words forming a unit in a sentence.

clue.text: Problem damaged church

parts.note: to hit something can damage it, a struck object

explanation.surface: Trouble arises because a church has been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or temporary difficulty that holds things up.

clue.text: Fish in a lake, something dull Bill caught

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: caught means the dull thing holds the bill inside it

parts.note: a bore is something tedious
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: An angler's tale: in a lake, Bill hooked something boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a person's name in the surface but is the account abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned tuna found in warm oceans.

clue.text: It could help you see, for example, girl — you may be enthralled

indicators.note: may be enthralled means a piece is held captive within the example abbreviation

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
ye is an old form of you
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Seeing a girl, for example, might leave you spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled' means held captive, so the old form of you sits within the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass is a single lens such as a monocle that aids vision.

clue.text: Person who went at the front of the conga must have been given inordinate trouble

definitions.text: Person who went at the front of the conga
definitions.meaning: the leader of a conga line literally guided a jolly dance
to have caused someone great bother, especially by evasive behaviour

explanation.surface: Whoever headed the conga line must have had a terrible time of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cause someone a lot of trouble, while literally describing leading a lively dance.

clue.text: El Cid struggling with fighters hiding in stronghold

indicators.note: hiding means the jumbled name conceals the fighters within it
struggling signals the hero's name writhes into a new letter order

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, is the UK's reserve fighting force

explanation.surface: The Spanish hero El Cid battles soldiers concealed within a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' turns EL CID into CIDEL, and 'hiding' places TA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, often one overlooking or protecting a city.

clue.text: Part of hospital to be facing both ways in African city

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

indicators.note: facing both ways means the word appears once backwards and once forwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital department ought to look in two directions in an African town.
explanation.definitionFit: Entebbe is a city in Uganda on Lake Victoria, home to the country's main airport.

clue.text: Joint in the bowels of hell somewhere in the East End

indicators.note: bowels are the innermost parts, so this takes the letters in the middle of the word

parts.note: Bow is a district in London's East End

explanation.surface: Someone finds a joint of meat in the depths of a hellish place in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinge joint between the upper and lower arm.

clue.text: Highly colourful gangster relating to plots?

parts.note: graphic means vivid or lurid in detail
Al Capone is the crossword's standard gangster

explanation.surface: A lurid gangster tale with a question about its storylines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plots' suggests stories but means graphs plotted on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphical means concerning graphs, and plotting points is how graphs are drawn.

clue.text: We, so ardent, so wrong, admitted mistakes in communication

indicators.note: wrong signals the preceding words are arranged incorrectly and must be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Passionate lovers who said something wrong have now owned up to errors in their messages.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat one's words is an idiom for retracting a statement and admitting one was mistaken.

clue.text: Time for children to get away from TV and sweat?

definitions.text: Time for children to get away from TV
definitions.meaning: the 9pm point after which UK broadcasters may show adult material
sweating is literally losing perspiration, shedding moisture

explanation.surface: Is it time the kids left the television and got some exercise?
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK the 9pm watershed marks when programmes unsuitable for children may be shown.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcasting cutoff is called the watershed, and to sweat is jokingly to have liquid shed.

clue.text: It sounds like northerner supports swimmers in the sea

indicators.note: it sounds like says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a Finn is a northerner from Finland, and backs means supports

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian supports the marine creatures, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Finbacks, or fin whales, are huge baleen whales of the open ocean.

clue.text: Go beyond with more than one maiden maybe, getting favourite upset

parts.note: a maiden is a cricket over with no runs, so several are overs

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, turns the word over so it reads upwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone oversteps the mark, courting several young women and upsetting their darling.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored; cricket is the British bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep is to exceed a limit or go further than is allowed.

clue.text: Sort of creature to get drunk, one out crossing green

indicators.note: crossing means the shortened word straddles another piece placed inside it
out says the following one is removed from the drunk word

parts.note: to inebriate is to make drunk
I is the Roman numeral for one
vert is the heraldic term for green

explanation.surface: Some animal gets tipsy, with one fellow crossing the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes away one letter, and 'crossing' has the shortened drunk word straddle the heraldic green.
explanation.definitionFit: An invertebrate is any animal lacking a backbone, such as an insect or worm.

clue.text: Crease in seat left after removal of foot

parts.note: the rump is the backside, what one sits on

indicators.note: after removal of says the word loses the following letters

explanation.surface: A wrinkle in the chair left once the foot was taken off it.
explanation.walkthrough: LEFT is written out, and the abbreviation FT is taken from it to leave LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumple is to crease or wrinkle cloth, or a rumple is such a fold.

clue.text: Decay of leftwinger overlooked by the likes of you and me

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooked by means the following piece sits above

parts.words: the likes of you and me
parts.note: you and me together are we
Trot is short for Trotskyist, a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist's decline goes unnoticed by ordinary people like us.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet rot is fungal decay of timber that has been kept damp.

clue.text: After damage by intense heat one building must be made lustrous

indicators.note: after says the heat damage comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: to burn is to damage with heat
I is the Roman numeral for one
a shed is a simple building

explanation.surface: After a fire, one building has to be polished up.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnished means polished until shiny, as with metal rubbed bright.

clue.text: This writer's time for reflection?

parts.note: this writer is I, and the setter is, so I'm
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An author's moment for contemplation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' is the setter saying I am.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is what one sees reflected in a mirror; the question mark flags the wordplay sense.

clue.text: Red shoes worn away at the sides

indicators.note: worn, as in battered out of shape, signals the remaining letters are rearranged
away at the sides says the outer letters are lost

parts.note: brogues are sturdy leather shoes with decorative perforations

explanation.surface: A pair of red shoes, scuffed at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the ends of BROGUES leaves ROGUE, which 'worn' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is French for red, and the name of a red cosmetic for the cheeks.

clue.text: Sharp weapon wounded girl

parts.note: cut means wounded with a blade
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is injured by a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword favoured by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Number joining the woman outside work who can't expect success?

indicators.note: outside means the woman surrounds the work

parts.note: her refers to a woman
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A man joins a woman in some activity but has no hope of winning.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of succeeding; the clue describes such a person.

clue.text: Son has stimulant after meal

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: A son takes a pick-me-up following dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, often a light one.

clue.text: Most scrawny little daughter that is needing stones put on

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
i.e., id est, means that is
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A thin little girl needs to gain some weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Weedy means thin and feeble, so the superlative is the thinnest and puniest.
